title: Annihilating scalar power in a kernel-minor Fitting ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be an $A$-module, let $d\ge0$ be an integer, and let $\pi:A^{\oplus d}\twoheadrightarrow M$ be a surjective $A$-linear map from the free module with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Write $I=I_0(\pi)\subset A$ for the ideal generated by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of all $d\times d$ matrices whose rows belong to $\ker\pi$, with $I=A$ when $d=0$, as in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Suppose $b\in A$ satisfies $bx=0$ for every $x\in M$. Then $b^d\in I$. In particular, if $a\in A$ and $m\ge1$ satisfy $b=a^m$, then $a^{md}\in I$ and $V(I)\subset V(a)$, where $V(I)$ is the set of prime ideals of $A$ containing $I$ and $V(a)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $a$.

source.place: Tag 0813, lemma-push-ideal, proof final sentence: a^(dm) lies in I since a^m annihilates the quotient; diagonal kernel-minor expansion, including rank zero (old item step 5).

proof.text: First, $M$ is generated by $\pi(e_1),\ldots,\pi(e_d)$: lift any $x\in M$ along the surjection and expand its lift in the given basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For each $i$, linearity and the annihilation hypothesis give $\pi(be_i)=b\pi(e_i)=0$. Hence every row $be_i$ belongs to $\ker\pi$.

source.place: Tag 0813 (lemma-push-ideal), final proof sentence; elementary expansion of the annihilating-power argument.

proof.text: If $d=0$, the convention $I=A$ gives $b^d=1\in I$. Suppose $d>0$. Let $D$ have rows $be_1,\ldots,be_d$, so $D_{ij}=b$ for $i=j$ and $D_{ij}=0$ otherwise. By the kernel-minor description in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] at $k=0$, $\det D$ is a generator of $I$. In the Leibniz formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the identity permutation contributes $b^d$; every other permutation moves some index $j$, and its product contains $D_{\sigma(j),j}=0$. Thus $\det D=b^d\in I$.

source.place: Tag 0813 (lemma-push-ideal), final proof sentence; elementary expansion of the annihilating-power argument.

proof.text: If $b=a^m$, the exponent identity $(a^m)^d=a^{md}$ gives $a^{md}\in I$. For $d=0$, $I=A$, so no prime ideal contains $I$ and $V(I)=\varnothing\subset V(a)$. For $d>0$, let $\mathfrak p\supset I$ be prime. Then $a^{md}\in\mathfrak p$ and $md\ge1$. If $a\notin\mathfrak p$, induction using primality ($uv\in\mathfrak p$ implies $u\in\mathfrak p$ or $v\in\mathfrak p$) shows $a^r\notin\mathfrak p$ for every $r\ge1$, a contradiction at $r=md$. Thus $a\in\mathfrak p$, proving $V(I)\subset V(a)$.

source.place: Tag 0813 (lemma-push-ideal), final proof sentence; elementary expansion of the annihilating-power argument.

Step 2: d=0 gives I=A. For d>0, D=b times the identity has rows in K, so its determinant generates I by the k=0 kernel-minor description in the statement of lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change. In the Leibniz formula (def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant) every non-identity permutation has a zero factor, so det D=b^d. This is a two-line computation, so the C1 exception applies. Step 3: primality and induction give a in p, with d=0 handled separately so a^0 is never used.
